extraction.name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH)
extraction.description: A suite of 23 challenging BIG-Bench tasks for which prior language model evaluations did not outperform the average human-rater.
extraction.creator: Mirac Suzgun, Nathan Scales, Nathanael Schärli, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yi Tay, Hyung Won Chung, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Denny Zhou, Jason Wei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Curated from the BIG-Bench benchmark by filtering tasks based on specific criteria to arrive at a clean, challenging, and tractable subset of 23 tasks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtered BIG-Bench tasks to exclude those with more than 3 subtasks, fewer than 100 examples, no human-rater baselines, non-multiple-choice/exact match metrics, tasks where models already beat human raters, and extremely difficult tasks. For all but three tasks, a random subset of 250 evaluation examples was taken.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The authors manually composed three chain-of-thought (CoT) exemplars for each task in BBH, prepending 'let's think step-by-step' to all CoT annotations.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Authors of the paper (for CoT exemplars). Original BIG-Bench human raters were an enlisted team, noted as not representative of the entire population.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The human-rater scores are not representative of the entire population.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Human-rater performance should be interpreted with care as scores are not fully representative of human performance, formatting/content changed multiple times, and raters could use external resources. Surpassing average human-rater performance should not be confused with true language understanding or reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the capabilities and limitations of large language models, specifically testing few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting on challenging tasks.
